expression: as.character(participant_id)
notes: Wave-prefixed running number (<year>_<OBS>) built in the tidier. KYRBS draws an independent cross-section each year and OBS restarts at 1 in every wave, so this key identifies one participant-observation and cannot be followed across years.

expression: as.character(YEAR)
notes: Annual survey round, 2005-2025. KYRBS is a repeated cross-section, so waves are collection occasions and not repeated measures on the same people.

expression: as.numeric(YEAR)
notes: Year of the annual survey administration; agrees with the wave directory in all 21 waves.

expression: coalesce(as.numeric(AGE_M) / 12, as.numeric(AGE))
notes: AGE_M is age in completed months (144-227) and gives finer resolution; it is absent in 2005 only, where integer AGE (12-18) is used instead. Neither carries sentinel codes in any wave.

expression: recode_values(as.numeric(SEX), 1 ~ "Male", 2 ~ "Female", default = "Unknown")
notes: Direction confirmed against height and weight at ages 17-18 (code 1 mean 175.0 cm / 71.2 kg; code 2 mean 161.9 cm / 56.0 kg). Administrative variable, complete in every wave.

expression: "South Korea"
notes: Nationally representative sample of Korean middle and high school students.
KYRBS collects no ethnicity, race or migration-background item in any wave.

No ethnicity item, so minority status cannot be derived.

expression:
case_when(
  YEAR == 2005 ~ "Unknown",
  as.numeric(E_SES) %in% c(1, 2) ~ "High",
  as.numeric(E_SES) == 3 ~ "Medium",
  as.numeric(E_SES) %in% c(4, 5) ~ "Low",
  .default = "Unknown"
)
notes: Single self-reported item on the family's economic standing, collapsed from the 5-point scale (high / upper-middle / middle / lower-middle / low). 2005 used a 4-point version with no middle category, which would put 57% of that wave in High against 29% in 2006; it is set to Unknown rather than forced onto the 5-point collapse. Subjective standing, not income or assets.

expression: if_else(YEAR == 2005, "Unknown", "Single-item self-reported household economic status (5-point, high to low)")
notes: 2005 used an incomparable 4-point version and is not carried into ses_household.

expression:
lookup_values(
  recode_values(
    as.numeric(E_EDU_M),
    1 ~ "Middle school graduate or less",
    2 ~ "High school graduate",
    3 ~ "College or university graduate or above",
    default = "Do not know"
  ),
  lookup_maternal_education,
  dataset_id = spec$dataset_id,
  target_variable = "maternal_education"
)
notes: Child-reported, and asked only of respondents who live with their mother; everyone else carries code 9999 (not asked) or 8888 (question block not administered, 2019 onwards) and lands on Unknown. Source code 3 combines junior-college and university graduates, so Bachelor degree or higher slightly overstates attainment for that group.

expression:
recode_values(
  as.numeric(E_EDU_F),
  c(1, 2) ~ "Secondary school or less",
  3 ~ "Bachelor degree or higher",
  default = "Unknown"
)
notes: Child-reported, asked only of respondents who live with their father. Same 4-category scale and the same junior-college caveat as maternal_education; code 4 (do not know) and the 8888/9999 skip codes become Unknown.

expression:
recode_values(
  pmax(
    ifelse(as.numeric(E_EDU_M) %in% 1:3, as.numeric(E_EDU_M), NA),
    ifelse(as.numeric(E_EDU_F) %in% 1:3, as.numeric(E_EDU_F), NA),
    na.rm = TRUE
  ),
  c(1, 2) ~ "Secondary school or less",
  3 ~ "Bachelor degree or higher",
  default = "Unknown"
)
notes: Highest of the two parents on the shared 3-level ordinal scale, ignoring do-not-know and skip codes. Where only one parent was asked about, that parent determines the value, so single-parent households are not systematically lower.

expression: recode_values(as.character(CTYPE), "대도시" ~ "Urban", "중소도시" ~ "Suburban", "군지역" ~ "Rural", default = "Unknown")
notes: KYRBS settlement-size stratifier, identically coded in all 21 waves: large city (metropolitan) / small-and-medium city / county. Mapping the middle level to Suburban is approximate - it denotes smaller cities rather than suburbs of a metropolitan area.

expression:
case_when(
  as.numeric(E_FM_F_1) == 8888 ~ "Unknown",
  as.numeric(E_FM_SF_2) == 2 | as.numeric(E_FM_SM_4) == 4 ~ "Step family",
  as.numeric(E_FM_F_1) == 1 & as.numeric(E_FM_M_3) == 3 ~ "Two biological/adoptive parents",
  as.numeric(E_FM_F_1) == 1 | as.numeric(E_FM_M_3) == 3 ~ "Single parent",
  as.numeric(E_FM_F_1) == 9999 & as.numeric(E_FM_M_3) == 9999 ~ "Other",
  .default = "Unknown"
)
notes: Derived from the household-roster tick boxes for father, step-father, mother and step-mother. The roster does not separate biological from adoptive parents. Step-parent boxes are absent in 2005, so step families there fall into the two-parent or single-parent categories. From 2019 the roster is asked of only part of the sample (code 8888, about 20%), which becomes Unknown.

expression:
case_when(
  YEAR == 2017 & as.numeric(INT_SP) == 1 ~ 0,
  YEAR == 2017 ~ as.numeric(INT_SP_WD) / 60,
  YEAR >= 2020 & as.numeric(INT_SPWD) == 1 ~ 0,
  YEAR >= 2020 ~ as.numeric(INT_SPWD_TM) / 60,
  .default = NA_real_
)
notes: Smartphone use on an average weekday. Minutes/60. The time item is gated by a preceding use/no-use question; when that gate says the respondent did not use, the time item is always missing in the source, so it is set to 0 rather than NA (verified exceptionless in every wave: gate = 1 gives 100% missing time, gate = 2 gives 100% present). Source column differs by era: INT_SP_WD in 2017, INT_SPWD_TM from 2020. The recall window also changed, from the past 30 days in 2017 to the past 7 days from 2020. No smartphone item was fielded in 2018-2019.

  YEAR >= 2020 ~ as.numeric(INT_SPWK_TM) / 60,

source_columns: YEAR, INT_SP, INT_SP_WD, INT_SP_WK, INT_SPWD, INT_SPWK, INT_SPWD_TM, INT_SPWK_TM
expression:
((case_when(
  YEAR == 2017 & as.numeric(INT_SP) == 1 ~ 0,
  YEAR == 2017 ~ as.numeric(INT_SP_WD) / 60,
  YEAR >= 2020 & as.numeric(INT_SPWD) == 1 ~ 0,
  YEAR >= 2020 ~ as.numeric(INT_SPWD_TM) / 60,
  .default = NA_real_
) *
  5) +
  (case_when(
    YEAR == 2017 & as.numeric(INT_SP) == 1 ~ 0,
    YEAR == 2017 ~ as.numeric(INT_SP_WK) / 60,
    YEAR >= 2020 & as.numeric(INT_SPWK) == 1 ~ 0,
    YEAR >= 2020 ~ as.numeric(INT_SPWK_TM) / 60,
    .default = NA_real_
  ) *
    2)) /
  7
notes: Smartphone use on a usual day. Weekday and weekend combined with the project's 5:2 weighted mean. See st_phone_wd.

expression:
recode_values(
  as.numeric(M_STR),
  1 ~ "A great deal",
  2 ~ "A lot",
  3 ~ "Some",
  4 ~ "A little",
  5 ~ "None at all",
  default = NA_character_
)
notes: Single item asked in all 21 waves: 'How much stress do you usually feel?', with five ordered options from a great deal to none at all. Mapped in rank order; the middle Korean anchors read closer to 'a little' and 'not much' than the dataschema wording, but the ordering is exact. No sentinel codes in any wave.

expression: recode_values(as.numeric(M_SUI_CON), 1 ~ "No", 2 ~ "Yes", default = NA_character_)
notes: 'In the past 12 months, have you seriously considered suicide?', asked in all 21 waves with a consistent 12-month recall and no sentinel codes.

expression:
case_when(
  as.numeric(M_SUI_ATT) == 1 ~ "No",
  as.numeric(M_SUI_ATT) == 2 ~ "Yes",
  as.numeric(M_SUI_ATT) == 9999 & as.numeric(M_SUI_CON) == 1 ~ "No",
  .default = NA_character_
)
notes: In the past 12 months, have you attempted suicide? Asked in all 21 waves with a consistent 12-month recall. In 2007-2010 the item was branched on the ideation question and only put to respondents who reported ideation; everyone else carries code 9999. That is a structural skip, not missing data - by the questionnaire logic those respondents did not attempt - so 9999 is mapped to No wherever ideation was also No (verified to hold exactly in all four affected waves). Reading 9999 as missing would restrict the denominator to ideators and lift the attempt rate for those waves to about 25% against roughly 5% either side.

recode_values(
  as.numeric(PR_BI),
  1 ~ "Much too thin",
  2 ~ "A bit too thin",
  3 ~ "About right",
  4 ~ "A bit too fat",
  5 ~ "Much too fat",
  default = NA_character_
)
notes: Single item asked in all 21 waves: 'What do you think of your body shape?' with options very thin / a bit thin / average / a bit fat / very fat, which line up one-to-one with the dataschema categories.

expression: 6 - as.numeric(PR_HD)
notes: Single item asked in 2006-2017, 2020 and 2023: 'How happy do you usually think you are?', with five options from very happy to very unhappy. Reversed so that higher means happier, giving 1-5 on the dataschema's higher-is-more-satisfied convention. Status is partial because the item measures subjective happiness rather than life satisfaction proper; the two correlate strongly but are not the same construct, so treat it cautiously when pooling with scored life-satisfaction instruments. No sentinel codes in any wave that fields it.
KYRBS does not field the Warwick-Edinburgh scale in any form. GAD-7 (2020-2024) is the only named instrument it uses.

expression:

  1 ~ "Excellent",
  2 ~ "Very good",
  3 ~ "Good",
  4 ~ "Fair",
  5 ~ "Poor",
  default = NA_character_
)
notes: Single item asked in all 21 waves: 'How do you think your usual health is?', with a symmetric five-point scale (very healthy / healthy / average / not healthy / very unhealthy) centred on average. Mapped in rank order onto the standard self-rated health anchors, so the middle category reads as Good here although the source wording is 'average'.
